history.summary: The oldest temple in Dakor, on the Gomti Ghat. Legend: the area was the dense Hidamba van; sage Dank Rishi (Dankmuni) did penance here, pleased Shiva, and Shiva left a replica of himself as a Ban lingam — hence 'Dankor', the town's old name. Krishna and Bhima are said to have visited the ashram; Dank Rishi invited Krishna to reside here, and Krishna promised to come in Kaliyuga — the origin of the Dakor Ranchhodrai tradition (see seq 1502). Served by Tapodhan Brahmins. MEDIA NOTE: the media image is a representative Shiva-lingam photo from image search; a verified photo of the temple exterior could not be found (verify). Coordinates approximate (verify).

name: Danknath Temple
town_description: Dakor is a small pilgrim city and municipality in Kheda district, Gujarat, in Thasra taluka, about 35 km east of Nadiad and 43 km northeast of Anand. Its name derives from ancient 'Dankor' (after Danknath Mahadev) and 'Khakhariya' (palash trees); the town sits by the holy Gomti lake and draws large Krishna-devotee crowds, especially on full-moon days.
